articles.headline: Google: AI Accelerates Discovery of Severe Vulnerabilities
articles.summary: A new report from Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) reveals that Artificial Intelligence is dramatically reshaping the vulnerability landscape. AI is accelerating the pace of vulnerability discovery, with monthly CVE disclosures doubling in 2026. These AI-discovered flaws are often more severe, with 50% leading to RCE, and are being weaponized by threat actors at a much faster rate. The report also highlights the growing attack surface of AI systems themselves.

articles.headline: Ransomware Data Exfiltration Surges 275%, Zscaler Reports
articles.summary: A new report from Zscaler ThreatLabz highlights a dramatic shift in ransomware tactics, with the volume of exfiltrated data increasing by over 275% year-over-year to nearly 900 terabytes. This indicates a strategic move from encryption-focused attacks to data theft for extortion. The report also notes that attackers are increasingly targeting employees in privileged roles and using generative AI to accelerate their operations. The freight & logistics and utilities sectors saw the largest growth in attacks.

articles.headline: China-Aligned Group TA419 Targets U.S. AI Policy Experts
articles.summary: A China-aligned cyber-espionage group, tracked as TA419 by Proofpoint, is conducting sophisticated phishing campaigns targeting U.S. experts in artificial intelligence policy. The attackers use elaborate impersonations of prominent officials and AI company employees to build rapport before luring targets to adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) phishing sites. The goal is to steal cloud account credentials, including passwords, MFA codes, and session cookies, to gather intelligence on U.S. AI strategy.

articles.headline: KillSec Ransomware Group Dismantled in International Takedown
articles.summary: A coordinated international law enforcement operation, dubbed 'Operation KillSwitch,' has successfully dismantled the prolific KillSec ransomware group. The operation, led by German authorities with support from Europol, resulted in the seizure of the group's servers, its dark web leak site, and 110 terabytes of stolen data. Investigators have identified the suspected main operator as a 16-year-old, and several arrests have been made across Europe.

articles.headline: Pentagon Data Breach Exposes Records of Over 3 Million
articles.summary: The U.S. Department of Defense has disclosed a massive data breach at its Defense Manpower Data Center (DMDC) that exposed the personal records of over 3 million individuals, including current and former military and civilian personnel. Attackers exploited a vulnerability in a file-sharing system and had undetected access for nine months, from October 2025 to July 2026, stealing sensitive data including Social Security numbers.

articles.headline: Cisco Patches Actively Exploited SD-WAN Zero-Day
articles.summary: Cisco has released urgent patches for a critical authentication bypass vulnerability, CVE-2026-76504, in its Catalyst SD-WAN Manager. The flaw, rated 9.8 on the CVSS scale, is being actively exploited to grant attackers unauthenticated administrative access to the system's API. CISA has added the vulnerability to its KEV catalog, and Cisco confirms there are no workarounds. Administrators are urged to upgrade their software immediately to prevent compromise.

articles.headline: Citrix NetScaler Zero-Days Under Mass Exploitation
articles.summary: Citrix has disclosed and patched two critical zero-day vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, in its NetScaler ADC and Gateway products. Both flaws, rated 9.5 CVSS, can lead to remote code execution and are under active, widespread exploitation by multiple threat actors, including suspected state-sponsored groups. Evidence suggests attackers were exploiting the flaws for at least three weeks before they were publicly disclosed, prompting CISA to add them to its KEV catalog and urge immediate patching.

articles.headline: Critical Fortinet FortiMail Zero-Day Exploited for RCE
articles.summary: Fortinet has disclosed a critical zero-day vulnerability, CVE-2026-104286, in its FortiMail secure email gateway. The flaw, which has a CVSS score of 9.8 and is under active exploitation, allows an unauthenticated attacker to write arbitrary files, leading to remote code execution. CISA has added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, mandating urgent action from federal agencies. While patches are pending, Fortinet has provided immediate workarounds, including disabling the IBE feature or restricting web access to the management interface.

articles.headline: Data Breaches at Healthcare & Professional Services Firms Disclosed
articles.summary: Several US-based organizations, including Modoc Medical Center and Blanchard Training & Development, have recently disclosed data breaches that occurred earlier in 2026. The public notifications reveal the exposure of sensitive data, including personal, financial, and protected health information (PHI) affecting thousands of individuals across the healthcare, legal, and professional services sectors.

articles.headline: Gartner Advises CISOs to Prioritize AI Risks, Preemptive Security
articles.summary: Technology research firm Gartner has released new guidance for CISOs, urging them to prioritize managing AI-related risks, budget for preemptive security capabilities, and treat all frontier AI models as a potential insider risk. The advice, published on September 30, comes as AI-augmented attacks accelerate, shrinking response times for defenders.

articles.headline: Google Report: AI Accelerates Vulnerability Discovery & Exploitation
articles.summary: A new report from Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) finds that Artificial Intelligence is significantly increasing the speed of both vulnerability discovery and subsequent exploitation. The number of disclosed vulnerabilities more than doubled in the first eight months of 2026, with a corresponding rise in the weaponization of high-risk flaws, particularly in network edge devices.

articles.headline: Dutch Security Institute Hacked via AI-Powered Zammad Zero-Days
articles.summary: The Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure (DIVD) was compromised by what it describes as an "agentic AI-powered attack." The sophisticated intrusion chained two zero-day vulnerabilities in the Zammad helpdesk software (CVE-2026-102489 and CVE-2026-102490) to achieve remote code execution and full system control, leading to a data breach.

articles.headline: Europol Dismantles KillSec Ransomware; Teenager Suspected Leader
articles.summary: An international law enforcement operation, codenamed Operation KillSwitch, has dismantled the infrastructure of the KillSec ransomware group. Led by German authorities and supported by Europol, the operation seized the group's darknet leak site and secured 110 TB of stolen data. A 16-year-old is suspected of being the group's main operator.

articles.headline: Russian APT Star Blizzard Evolves Phishing with 'RedFlick' Technique
articles.summary: The Russian APT group Star Blizzard (FSB Centre 18) has adopted a new, more efficient malware delivery technique called "RedFlick" to deploy its CosmicPulse backdoor. The new method streamlines phishing campaigns against Ukraine-linked targets, including NGOs and journalists, by requiring only a single user interaction to initiate the infection chain.

articles.headline: Cisco Patches Actively Exploited SD-WAN Auth Bypass Zero-Day
articles.summary: Cisco has patched a critical authentication bypass zero-day (CVE-2026-76504, CVSS 9.8) in its Catalyst SD-WAN Manager. The flaw, caused by improper URI handling, allows remote unauthenticated attackers to gain admin access. CISA has added it to the KEV catalog, urging immediate patching as there are no workarounds.

articles.headline: Critical Citrix Zero-Day Exploited for Weeks Before Discovery
articles.summary: A critical memory overflow vulnerability (CVE-2026-88772) in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway was exploited by suspected state-sponsored actors for over three weeks before public disclosure. Attackers deployed the WHIPSHOT web shell and SLAPSHOT tunneling tool, targeting government and financial institutions across North America and Europe. CISA has added the flaw to its KEV catalog, mandating immediate patching.

articles.headline: NetScaler Zero-Days CVE-2026-88771 & CVE-2026-88772 Actively Exploited
articles.summary: Citrix has disclosed two critical zero-day vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, in its NetScaler appliances, which are being actively exploited in the wild. The vulnerabilities, both rated with a CVSS score of 9.5, can lead to denial of service or remote code execution. Threat actors have been observed exploiting these flaws since at least August 21, 2026, to deliver web shells, establish initial access, and maintain persistence. Unit 42 analysis identified over 50,000 exposed NetScaler instances and detailed two distinct attack patterns, one involving a crafted DTLS packet and another using a three-stage log poisoning technique to achieve RCE. Immediate patching is critical.
